certificate.title: Claude Cheat Sheet 2026: 17 Tips to Stop Using Claude Like It's 2025 Completion

course.description: A comprehensive 17-point cheat sheet covering everything from picking the right model, to Cowork setup, connectors, Skills, voice dictation, and the right tool for images/search/video. Adapted from Ruben Hassid's LinkedIn post.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Claude Cheat Sheet 2026: 17 Tips to Stop Using Claude Like It's 2025.

lessons.content:
Claude is not a single chatbot. It's six distinct surfaces, each designed for different work:

- **Chat** — quick questions, brainstorming, one-off tasks
- **Projects** — persistent workspaces with uploaded files and custom instructions
- **Code** — Claude Code for terminal-based software engineering
- **Cowork** — desktop agent that reads your local files, creates docs, and runs autonomously
- **Skills** — reusable slash-command workflows you build once and trigger forever
- **Connectors** — live integrations with Slack, Gmail, Drive, Notion, and 50+ other tools

**If you don't code, Cowork should be your go-to.**

Most people only use Chat. That's like buying a Swiss Army knife and only using the toothpick. Identify which surface fits your task before you start typing.
lessons.title: Claude Isn't 1 Tool — It's 6

activities.title: Pick the Model Before the Prompt

lessons.content:
Different models are optimized for different tasks. Choose before you type:

| Model | Best For |
|-------|----------|
| **Opus 4.8** | Thinking, analyzing, planning — deep reasoning tasks |
| **Sonnet 4.6** | Grammar, brainstorming, formatting — everyday creative work |
| **Haiku 4.6** | Bulk tasks at 1M input tokens — high-volume, low-cost processing |

**Rule of thumb:** If the task requires judgment or multi-step reasoning, use Opus. If it's formatting, drafting, or light editing, Sonnet is faster and cheaper. If you're processing a large batch, Haiku handles massive context at a fraction of the cost.
lessons.title: Pick the Model Before the Prompt

lessons.content:
For complex analysis, you can force Opus to think harder:

1. Open the **model selector** in the chat interface
2. Select **Opus 4.8**
3. Turn on **Effort → High**

This forces an internal monologue — Claude will reason through the problem step-by-step before responding. It takes longer but produces significantly better results for tasks like:

- Financial analysis with multiple variables
- Strategic planning documents
- Complex code architecture decisions
- Multi-step research synthesis

**When to skip it:** Don't use High Effort for simple questions or formatting tasks — you'll burn tokens for no benefit.
lessons.title: Toggle High Effort on Opus

lessons.content:
Cowork is available on Desktop + Pro plans. It's a fundamentally different experience from Chat:

- **Reads your local files** — no more copy-pasting documents into the chat
- **Creates and edits documents** directly on your machine
- **Runs for minutes autonomously** while you grab coffee
- **Maintains context** across a working session

If you're doing real work — writing reports, analyzing spreadsheets, drafting memos — Cowork is where you should be. Chat is for quick questions. Cowork is for getting things done.
lessons.title: Cowork > Chat for Serious Work

lessons.content:
You don't need a novel-length prompt. Write 29 words:

> "I want to [task] so that [goal]. Read the files first. Ask me questions via AskUserQuestion before executing."

That's it. This prompt pattern does three things:

1. **States the task and goal** — Claude knows what and why
2. **Points to context** — "Read the files first" tells Claude to gather information before acting
3. **Forces clarification** — "Ask me questions before executing" prevents Claude from guessing wrong

The longer your prompt, the more likely Claude is to latch onto the wrong detail. Short, clear instructions with the right context files will outperform a wall of text every time.
lessons.title: Stop Writing 500-Word Prompts

lessons.content:
Create this folder structure in your Cowork workspace:

```
ABOUT ME/       → Your identity, rules, preferences, tone of voice
TEMPLATES/      → Reusable patterns (email formats, report structures, analysis frameworks)
CLAUDE OUTPUTS/ → Where Claude saves all deliverables
```

**Why this works:** Once Claude knows who you are (ABOUT ME), has your patterns (TEMPLATES), and knows where to save (CLAUDE OUTPUTS), your prompts drop to 10 words. Instead of re-explaining your role, style, and format every session, Claude reads the folders and already knows.

**Pro tip:** Put your job title, team context, writing style preferences, and any "never do this" rules in ABOUT ME. The more specific, the better.
lessons.title: Build 3 Folders Inside Cowork

lessons.content:
Go to **Settings → Cowork → Edit Global Instructions** and paste something like:

> "Read ABOUT ME first. Save deliverables in CLAUDE OUTPUTS. Use AskUserQuestion when unclear. Don't over-explain."

These instructions apply to every Cowork session automatically. You set them once and never think about them again.

**What to include in Global Instructions:**
- Where to find your context files
- Where to save outputs
- When to ask vs. when to proceed
- Tone preferences ("be concise", "use bullet points", "no fluff")
- Any hard rules ("never delete files", "always confirm before sending")
lessons.title: Set Global Instructions Once

lessons.content:
Connectors let Claude read your live data from other tools — zero copy-paste required:

**Available connectors include:** Slack, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Figma, Granola, and 50+ others.

**How to enable:**
1. Go to Claude settings
2. Find the Connectors section
3. Toggle on the services you use
4. Authorize access

Once connected, Claude can read your emails and Slack messages mid-conversation. Instead of copying a thread into the chat, just say "check my last 5 emails from the CFO" and Claude pulls them live.

**This is free.** There's no reason not to turn them on.
lessons.title: Turn On Connectors (They're Free)

lessons.content:
Add this to your prompts: **"Ask me questions via AskUserQuestion before executing."**

What happens:
- Claude **stops guessing** what you want
- It generates a **form with clarifying questions**
- You click your answers
- Claude executes with precision

This single addition eliminates the #1 frustration with AI: it doing something you didn't ask for. Instead of a 3-round back-and-forth correcting mistakes, Claude gets it right the first time because it asked first.

**Best for:** Complex tasks where requirements are ambiguous — report generation, data analysis, document drafting.
lessons.title: Force AskUserQuestion in Every Prompt

lessons.content:
Setup takes 3 minutes:

1. Open **Excel**
2. Go to **Insert → Get Add-ins**
3. Search **"Claude by Anthropic"**
4. Click **Add**
5. **Sign in** with your Claude account
6. Use **Ctrl+Option+C** (Mac) or **Ctrl+Alt+C** (Windows) to open the Claude panel

Claude now knows what cell D14 actually contains. You can ask it to:
- Explain formulas in plain English
- Write new formulas based on your description
- Analyze data patterns across your spreadsheet
- Generate pivot table suggestions
- Debug formula errors

**For finance teams:** This is a game-changer for model review, variance analysis, and ad-hoc data questions without leaving your workbook.
lessons.title: Install Claude in Excel

lessons.content:
**Plugins** add pre-built capabilities to Claude. Browse them at claude.com/plugins:

- Categories: Sales, Marketing, Legal, **Finance**, Data, Product, Support, and more
- Each plugin adds new skills and slash commands
- Type `/` in the chat to see available commands

**Skills** are your own custom slash commands — they replace your prompt library entirely:

1. Turn any repeat workflow into a slash command
2. Example: Type `/negotiation-prep` + one line of context
3. Claude pulls from Gmail, Slack, Granola automatically
4. Drafts the deliverable. Done.

**The difference:** Plugins are pre-built by others. Skills are workflows you build yourself for your specific needs. Both save massive time by eliminating repetitive prompting.
lessons.title: Install Plugins & Build Skills

lessons.content:
The single biggest upgrade to your Claude output: **feed your files, not just prompts.**

A mediocre prompt with great context files will outperform a perfect prompt with no context every time. Claude's strength is synthesizing information — but it can only work with what you give it.

**What to upload:**
- The actual spreadsheet, memo, or document you're working on
- Examples of previous outputs you liked
- Your company's style guide or templates
- Relevant background documents

**In Cowork:** Just point Claude to your local folders. In Projects: upload files to the project knowledge base. In Chat: attach files to individual messages.

The game is context, not prompting.
lessons.title: Context > Prompts — Feed Your Files

lessons.content:
Stop writing 500 words describing your writing style. Instead:

**Paste 3 examples of posts/emails/reports you wrote. Say: "Write like this."**

Claude copies your voice faster from examples than from any amount of description. This works because:

1. **Examples encode implicit rules** — your sentence length, vocabulary, tone, structure
2. **Descriptions are lossy** — "professional but approachable" means different things to different people
3. **Pattern matching is what LLMs do best** — you're playing to Claude's strength

**For finance teams:** Paste 3 previous board memos and say "write the Q3 memo in this style." Paste 3 variance commentaries and say "write commentary for these new variances." The output will match your team's voice immediately.
lessons.title: Examples > Prescriptions

activities.title: Know When NOT to Use Claude

lessons.content:
Claude is excellent at text, reasoning, and code. But for some tasks, other tools are simply better:

**Images → Use ChatGPT Image (with Thinking)**
Claude doesn't generate realistic images (yet). If you need image generation, ChatGPT with its image model is the current leader.

**Real-time search → Use Grok**
Grok is connected to X/Twitter and covers 99% of real-time search needs. If you need today's news, live data, or trending topics, Grok gets there faster.

**Videos → Use Google Veo-4**
For video generation, Google's Veo-4 is the right tool right now.

**The principle:** Right tool, right job. Stop wasting tokens asking Claude to do things other tools handle better. Use Claude for what it's best at — reasoning, writing, analysis, and code — and route everything else to the specialist tool.
lessons.title: Know When NOT to Use Claude
